name: The enhanced game's rules
description: The FPS/TPS action RPG's rules as the rules package specifies them: its configuration and profiles and its actor sheet.

switches.streamer: streamer mode for this run: network addresses and ports, the user's folder in paths and any join code hidden wherever they would show on screen (the log window too; the log files keep them). The setting is the platform's, the same in every game, and kept from the game's options
switches.sandbox: run the research sandbox profile (the shipping profile refuses: fail closed)
switches.skill-tempo-off: turn the Abilities' tempo channel off for the run (Melee and Brawl no longer quicken the swing, the recovery and the block; data/combat/skill.json)
switches.skill-contest: turn the Abilities' contest on contact on for the run, a research comparator and no default (Dexterity + Melee against the defender's Dexterity, + Melee while he guards, + Dodge while he dodges; data/combat/skill.json)
switches.celerity-curve-oneone: play Celerity on 1.1's curve (move x1.5 to x3.5, attack x1.1 to x1.5 by rank; effects.ned; no flurry) in place of the default split (data/rules/powers.json)
switches.celerity-curve-tempo: play Celerity as before, all tempo: (1 + rank)x movement and attack speed and no flurry, in place of the default split (a body tempo of (1 + rank)^0.5 and a flurry of the same, the blows each swing that lands on a body carries; data/rules/powers.json)
switches.celerity-attack-off: turn Celerity's attack speed and flurry off for the run (its movement alone; the attack's model is provisional; data/rules/powers.json)
switches.severance-off: turn severance off for the run: nothing is cut off and every body contact stops the blade, the earlier build's harm (severance otherwise runs: a blade's blow whose harm after soak reaches a part's threshold cuts it off and goes on with what its swing has left; data/rules/severance.json)
switches.contact-stop-off: blades no longer stop where they stop, for the run: the earlier build's contact (the blade through bodies, one contact per swing and person, a shield's or a wall's stop cut short at once; data/combat/weapons.json's stop)
switches.rebound-fixed: a blocked blade's rebound as before, for the run: 0.15 m for every blow, no recoil through the arm, no attacker's stun, the guard rising when the busy time ends (data/combat/weapons.json's stop.scaled)
switches.rebound-small: the blocked blade's rebound and the arm's recoil at half their size, for the run (the film's small; data/combat/weapons.json's stop.scaled)
switches.rebound-stun-after: the attacker's stun after a blocked blow counted from the end of the blocked swing's busy time, for the run: the stun on top of the whole swing's time (data/combat/weapons.json's stop.scaled.stun)
switches.rebound-large: the blocked blade's rebound and the arm's recoil at 1.8 times their size, for the run (the film's large; data/combat/weapons.json's stop.scaled)
switches.dodge-dexterity-off: turn the dodge's Dexterity link off for the run (every body's burst a human's, to measure the Dodge Ability's channel alone; data/combat/skill.json)
switches.severance-angle-off: severance without the blow's angle, for the run: every blow's whole harm after soak counts toward cutting, the test (the angle band is still measured; data/rules/severance.json's angle)
switches.severance-melee-off: severance without Melee's edge, for the run: each angle band's own cut share, whatever the attacker's Melee (data/rules/severance.json's melee_edge)
switches.armor-off: turn armour off for the run: it soaks nothing, the harm of before armour (what people wear is still kept; armour otherwise adds the dice of the pieces over the struck part to its soak; data/combat/armor.json)
switches.guard-off: turn the earlier build's guard off for the run: attack refused while blocking, no parry window, no clash, no automatic guard direction, a guard met holding at once (the earlier build's guard; the guard otherwise runs: data/combat/guard.json)
switches.guard-sight-off: the automatic guard turns toward any threat in its arc for the run, the earlier build's (otherwise only toward a threat its owner can see, by perception's own test: the rules package)
switches.guard-sight-body: the player's automatic guard sees by the body's facing for the run, as everyone else does (otherwise by the player's view: a 55-degree cone round the look direction, from the eyes in first person and from behind them, where the camera stands, in third)
switches.flurry-compressed: play Celerity's extra blows as before: every extra blow a swing carries resolved at once on its one contact (a shield stops all, nothing else can), in place of the default (each extra blow its own strike at its own moment, landing only where the blade's line still meets the target then; data/rules/flurry.json)
switches.flurry-off: Celerity without extra blows for the run: pure tempo (the body quickened, each swing one blow), in place of the default geometric flurry (data/rules/flurry.json)
switches.flurry-swing-spacing: the geometric flurry's extra blows spread evenly through the rest of the swing in place of data/rules/flurry.json's fixed spacing (0.04 s), to compare
switches.guard-technique-off: the guard's technique term off for the run: a guard holds by its Strength alone and a parry turns nothing (the guard's contest otherwise adds technique, Dexterity's dice and Melee: data/combat/guard.json)
switches.guard-melee-off: Melee out of the guard's technique for the run: technique is Dexterity's dice alone, so Melee counts in no guard verdict (its fourth lane isolated for the Melee ablations)
switches.contest-dexterity-performed: with skill-contest: the defence's Dexterity counts only alongside a performed defence, a guard raised or a dodge in its burst (otherwise always, the rules package decides)
switches.flurry-motion: show each extra blow of a Celerity swing as a re-strike: the blade pulled back a short way from the bite and driven through the strike again, arriving at the checked line at the blow's moment (data/rules/flurry.json's motion; off by default; it changes the picture, not the check)
switches.flurry-spacing-80ms: the geometric flurry's extra blows 0.08 s apart in place of the data's 0.04 s, to compare
switches.flurry-spacing-120ms: the geometric flurry's extra blows 0.12 s apart in place of the data's 0.04 s, to compare
switches.flurry-spacing-160ms: the geometric flurry's extra blows 0.16 s apart in place of the data's 0.04 s, to compare
switches.blow-quality-off: blow quality off for the run: every contact deals its whole damage potential whatever the work it could do, the hilt cuts as the blade, severance's cut share is the angle's (the earlier build's harm; the quality is still measured and recorded; otherwise a contact's potential is scaled by its quality, data/rules/quality.json)
switches.blow-quality-hilt-off: the hilt alone off for the run: a blade's contact at its hilt keeps its class's kind (otherwise one nearer the guard than data/rules/quality.json's hilt limit is bashing)
switches.brain-range-off: the duelling brain without range keeping for the run: a blade fighter swings from wherever it is, a clinch included (otherwise it steps back out of a clinch, or round its foe when pinned, before it swings again)
switches.guard-solver-off: the guard's arm solver off for the run: a lone blade's raised guard keeps the earlier build's composed pose (otherwise, it is driven across the path of a blow its owner sees, within the arm's reach and a hand's speed, and a guard met gives and springs back; data/combat/guard.json's arm_solver and give)
switches.attack-spin: 1.1's tap-and-hold for the run: quick blows in turn, the spin attack when attack is held, a blow begun on release (an earlier build exactly), in place of directional attacks (otherwise the blow's direction is chosen at the press - automatic by the crosshair on the foe, the mouse's flick or the movement keys, the setting attackDirection - held ready while attack is held and struck on release; no spin: data/combat/directions.json)
switches.guard-skill-off: the guard by skill off for the run: every fighter guards with the earlier build's numbers, its hand's speed, its read time and the duelling brain's chances whatever its Dexterity and Melee (otherwise data/combat/guard.json's skill curve)
switches.brain-parry-fixed: the duelling brain's parry as before, for the run: 0.25 s before the blow's strike mark whatever its own swing (otherwise timed by its hand's travel and chosen only when its own swing will be over in time: data/combat/guard.json's brain_parry)
switches.stagger-oneone: the flinch as before, for the run: a wounding blow plays 1.1's whole hurt at most once in 3.5 s, no push of the upper body, no stagger from an overpowered guard (otherwise the stagger when hit: data/combat/guard.json's stagger)
switches.rebound-two-thirds: the blocked blade's rebound and the arm's recoil at the earlier build's sizes and a parry twice the held, for the run (an earlier build made them 1.5 times, a parry 1.4 times that; data/combat/weapons.json's stop.scaled)
switches.rebound-stun-at-meeting: the attacker's stun after a blocked blow counted from the meeting, as before, for the run (an earlier build counts it from the end of the blocked swing's busy time by default; data/combat/weapons.json's stop.scaled.stun)
switches.swings-oneone: 1.1's own side blows for the run: the forehand and the backhand as 1.1 animates them, the forehand coming down diagonally from its loop over the head and the backhand low, in place of their sweeps brought level at the chest (OneOneStitched.SwingHeight)
switches.stagger-hurt-clip: an alias of stagger-hurt-short (the earlier build's name for it, kept so a tape that names it replays the same)
switches.stagger-push-only: the stagger as the push alone, as before, for the run: the swing cut short, the guard lowered and the body busy for 0.3-0.6 s by the blow's impulse, the chest pushed, the body upright and in reach - no 1.1 hurt clip (by default 1.1's hurt clip played whole: data/combat/guard.json's stagger.hurt)
switches.stagger-hurt-short: the stagger with 1.1's hurt clip cut at 0.3-0.6 s by the blow's impulse, for the run (the earlier build's stagger-hurt-clip; by default the clip plays whole, 1.3 s: data/combat/guard.json's stagger.hurt)
switches.pace-off: the duelling brain's constant aggression for the run: no pause between its runs of blows, an arena spec's brain.pace included (otherwise every fighter with a sheet keeps its kind of person's pace - townsfolk, guards and the watch, Kindred and the szlachta - a run of one or two blows then a pause drawn from its range: data/combat/guard.json's brain_pace)
switches.blade-guard-everyone: every duelling brain guards with a blade (or fists) by its skill for the run, as (otherwise a fighter below data/combat/guard.json's skill.blade_guard_least, Melee or Brawl bare-handed, raises no blade or fists to block or parry, only a shield; the player's own guard is unchanged)
switches.combat-tempo-off: the earlier build's pace for the run: no global combat tempo, every blow at 1.1's timing under Melee's and Celerity's rates (otherwise every fighter's swing and recovery play at data/combat/pace.json's tempo.global, 0.70, or --combat-tempo's: humans moving at human speeds)
switches.fighting-pace-off: no fighting pace for the run: a body runs and sprints through its own blow, as earlier (otherwise a body whose blow is swinging or held ready moves at most data/combat/pace.json's fighting_pace, 1.8 m/s)
switches.rush-unpaced: rushing creatures keep their own pace through their blows, for the run: the bodies whose sheet is one of data/combat/pace.json's rush_unpaced templates (the szlachta) are not held to the fighting pace while they swing (otherwise every body is)
switches.dodge-paced: the dodge at data/combat/pace.json's pace for the run: a human's 1 m burst in 0.35 s, not 0.30, and the recovery 0.45 s, not 0.40 (pace.json's dodge.use makes it the default; off by default)
switches.shield-read-off: no shield read for the run: a duelling brain aims its blows at a shield-bearer as, whatever its Melee (otherwise, by data/combat/guard.json's shield_read, a skilled brain aims a blow over or under the foe's shield as he holds it: skill tells against a shield)
switches.window-from-windup: the earlier build's active windows for the run: a wind-up's blow swept for contact, and drawn by the swing's arc, from where the blade leaves the ready pose (otherwise from where the strike proper begins: the side blows' blade level, the overhead's top, the thrust's start forward; data/combat/weapons.json's activeWindow.strikeStarts)
switches.blows-on-moving-hips: a blow struck while moving plays on the upper body over the walk's or run's hips for the run, as before, and its sweep tilts (from the right it rises and turns, the thrust goes low and left) (otherwise, by default, it keeps its upper body turned as the blow's own hips turn it: ActionHips, ENGINE_SANDBOX)
switches.guards-one-blow: the guards and the watchmen keep 1.1's one side blow for the run (the earlier build's three directions: from the right, overhead, the thrust), in place of the left lent them (Christof's flattened backhand with its wind-up into the left ready pose, played on their own bodies at their weapon's times)
switches.aim-at-press: the duelling brain's aim worked out once, at the press, for the run, as before (otherwise, it keeps its blow aimed at its foe's body through the blow, from where both stand and as the foe's pose has him each tick, as a player's look follows his foe: against a low foe closing during the wind-up the press's aim passed over his head; Combat/SwingAim.cs)
switches.blow-hips-upright: the composed blows (the flattened side blows, the guards' lent left and every wind-up) sampled with their hips held upright and the turn and bow they carried put on the bones above and below them, for the run (so a blow struck while the body moves keeps its turn and bow; off by default - blows-moving-hips does it for every blow in the pose evaluator, and the two together measure the same as it alone; Animation/StitchedClips.cs StitchHips)
switches.foes-uniform: the earlier build's fighters for the run: every fighter moves as the human (a foe preset's, an arena fighter's or a scenario actor's movement is passed over: no template speeds, no neonate or elder) and every duelling brain closes as the duelling brain does (approach oneone passed over: no 1.1 manoeuvre); for the unchanged check and for comparing with 1.1's szlachta as 1.1 has them
switches.shield-at-bow-off: a duelling brain with a shield does not raise it against a bow drawn and aimed at it, for the run (the earlier build's brain: it answers only a blow in reach; by default it raises its shield toward an archer whose bow is drawn to a quarter and aimed within 12 degrees of its chest within 40 m and 80 degrees of its facing, after its block's reaction, and holds it while the bow stays so; src/Vitomir.Platform/Combat/ShieldAgainstBow.cs)
switches.bow-look-off: an archer keeps the look for the run: his melee stance and his sword in hand while the bow is out (by default he is posed and drawn with 1.1's bow - Christof's stand_bow, walk_bow, run_bow, the shot chrisAttackBow played by the draw, hurt_bow, and the longBow's model; the pose moves his hit volumes; src/Vitomir.Platform/Combat/BowLook.cs)
switches.bow-aim-off: the player's bow as before, for the run: attack held raises and draws it without aim, the arrow leaves along the line to the crosshair's point with the module's spread by Range, and every archer plays 1.1's shot clip as it is (by default aim, Q, raises the bow into the ready pose composed from 1.1's full draw, attack held while aiming draws, the player's arrow leaves along the line to the crosshair's point with no spread, and every archer's draw takes its Range's time; src/Vitomir.Platform/Control/PlayerBow.cs)
switches.bow-solve-on: the player's arrow is launched at the angle that carries it to the crosshair's point at the draw reached, for the run (by default it leaves along the straight line to that point and drops as a real arrow does; the setting bowAimSolve; src/Vitomir.Platform/Control/PlayerBow.cs)
switches.brain-straight: the duelling brain closes straight at its foe whatever stands between them, for the run, as before did (by default, only while the straight line to its foe meets the level - a wall - it runs the navigation mesh's route round it, facing the way; a clear line changes nothing; src/Vitomir.Platform/Combat/DuelRoutes.cs)
switches.accel-ramp: the player starts and stops on the earlier build's fixed ramp, as every other body does, for the run (by default the player's ground speed follows a critically damped spring toward the wished one, its half-life its movement profile's StartStopHalfLife - the human 0.2 s, the neonate 0.15, the elder 0.1 -, the air keeping AirControl times the ramp; the ramp is AccelerationCapacity up and BrakingDeceleration down; a tape without the note accel replays on the ramp; src/Vitomir.Platform/Bodies/BodyMotor.Spring.cs)
switches.arrows-heavy: the war arrow is the heavy war arrow, as before (87.5 g at 53.3 m/s from the war bow at full draw), for the run (by default the items set's long bow bow_long_x01 rated 120 lbf, 123.2 J stored, looses its war arrow of 54.5 g at about 58.2 m/s and its hunting arrow of 57.7 g at about 56.6 m/s; a tape with a bow and without the note arrows replays with this arrow; Data/combat/ranged.json)
switches.landing-slide: the player's landings on the spring as before, for the run: the speed across a landing keeps is taken up by the spring, so a landing on a slope slides on (0.19 m on a 39-42 degree ramp) (by default a landing keeps only the speed along the way the player is asked to go, up to the pace asked - none when nothing is asked -, the rest dropped at once; a tape on the spring without the note landing replays with this switch; src/Vitomir.Platform/Bodies/BodyMotor.cs)
